text:
nina: quick RFC follow-up — sketching a "live compaction shim" for microbatch-heavy inference workloads. goal: reclaim fragmented slab space without stalling inflight microbatches or blowing tail latency. thoughts?

sam: can you spell out the failure modes you care about? is this about steady-state fragmentation or bursty reclaim during low qps windows?

nina: mostly steady-state fragmentation + slow accumulation from many small evicts. current full-compaction pauses are killing 95/99 P50s for some tenants. idea: incremental compaction applied per-shard with a handshake so we never preempt an active batch.
jules: curious how this interacts with KV cache — we compact slabs that may contain pinned kv entries? we need a move/replace protocol.
nina: right. basic approach: mark candidate ranges, start a background walker that copies live objects into fresh slabs, patching live pointers via a short-lived indirection. do it in small quanta aligned to microbatch boundaries.
eric: indirection adds cost. how do we avoid amplifying latency for reads in the fast path?
maria: maybe keep indirection only for compaction epochs and remap on a per-microbatch commit. microbatch commit point is natural: we drain per-request KVCaches, swap in remapped pages between batches.
nina: exactly. handshake proto (sketch):
```
# coordinator -> shard agent
request_compact(shard_id, epoch_id, target_reclaim_frac=0.15, quantum_ms=5)
# agent replies ack/deny. if ack -> agent performs small steps between batch boundaries
# on step: move N objects, publish remap table for epoch_id\napply_remap(epoch_id) -> quick apply at next safe microbatch boundary
```

sam: sounds reasonable. two concerns: (1) remap table memory overhead, (2) correctness if a microbatch spans the apply point. need a fast-check to ensure no pointers are mid-update.
jules: can do a lightweight barrier: a small epoch-bit per request context. requests take current_epoch bit; remap apply toggles epoch after in-flight count goes to zero. similar to RCU but per-shard and bounded.
eric: how do we measure when to start compaction? heuristics based on fragmentation ratio alone are noisy. we should use per-shard allocation churn + reclaim velocity. maybe start only when reclaimable_bytes / total_bytes > T and allocation_rate < R for last 10s.
maria: +1. also include tenant-priority gating so high-SLA tenants never get compaction on their hot shards. default: tenant_level <= standard triggers compaction; premium tenants require manual opt-in.
ci-bot: ci: related perf test job queued -> perf/compaction-live/epoch-smoke (id: 3291)

nina: good catch on tenant gating. for remap overhead we can compress remap table by ranges and only publish diffs. quantum_ms and objects-per-step knobs let us tune background throughput vs tail.
eric: add a global throttler that listens to token-bucket derived from observed tail latency. if 99th climbs, throttle compaction to 0.
sam: UX question: config surface — we need a per-shard policy: {enabled, target_frac, quantum_ms, priority_class, tenant_gate}. plumb through admin console + runtime API.
jules: testing plan: synthetic microbatch workload + mixed tenant profiles. measure p50/p95/p99 before/after, plus reclaimed bytes, remap table memory, and CPU overhead.
maria: one more: ensure compatibility with existing offload path. if pages are staged out to host, compaction should prefer to pull back live objects before move to avoid double-copy.
nina: noted. action items: i'll open a draft RFC PR with the handshake proto, config schema, and perf experiment matrix. tagging @sam @jules @eric for review.
sam: +1 — include a small flag to force-apply in dev env.
jules: +1 — add correctness checklist (rcu counters, remap atomicity tests).
eric: thanks — would like a perf run once you have a prototype.
maria: I'll sketch tenant gating rules and a console mockup.
ci-bot: ci: perf job 3291 started -> 10m ETA
nina: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready. :mouth_open:
